outcome: Control zones sit behind ruggedised, protocol-aware boundaries with vendor access brokered and logged rather than left as a standing rule.
overview: Utility control networks were built to be separate and are not any more: historians feed corporate reporting, vendors need remote access for maintenance, and the air gap has become a firewall rule somebody added years ago. Fortinet OT Security places ruggedised inspecting boundaries between control zones and the corporate network, with protocol awareness for industrial traffic so a rule can distinguish a read from a command. The constraint that shapes everything is that plant availability outranks security change, so the design is built around passive discovery and windows measured in months.

benefits.text: Control zones are separated from corporate networks by an inspecting boundary that understands industrial protocols
benefits.limits: Protocol awareness covers the protocols on the supported list; proprietary or serial-bridged traffic may be visible as a flow and not as a command

benefits.text: Vendor remote access becomes a brokered, logged path rather than a standing rule
benefits.limits: Depends on plant vendors accepting a brokered path, which is a contractual conversation as much as a technical one

benefits.text: An asset inventory of the control estate emerges from passive observation rather than active scanning
benefits.limits: Passive discovery sees what talks; a device that is silent during the observation window will not appear, and the inventory must say so

residency: Ruggedised appliances and their logs remain inside the plant or the utility’s own data centre; no control-system telemetry needs to leave the operator’s estate

notFor.situation: A plant with a dedicated industrial monitoring platform already deployed and staffed
notFor.why: Passive discovery and protocol visibility are what that platform already provides; a second one duplicates the sensor estate

notFor.situation: A control network with a genuine, audited air gap and no remote maintenance requirement
notFor.why: There is no crossing to inspect, and introducing a device introduces a change where none was needed

scope:
Model: Redington solutions engineering with an accredited Fortinet OT implementation partner, working to the plant’s own change process · Duration: 16–24 weeks per plant, driven by outage windows rather than by engineering effort
Support model: Vendor hardware and subscription support with an agreed replacement term appropriate to plant criticality; Redington coordinates the vendor case.
1) Discover — passive observation across a full operating cycle, asset inventory with stated limits
2) Design — zone and conduit model agreed with plant engineering and the control system vendors
3) Insert — first conduit boundary in an agreed window, rehearsed beforehand on a bench
4) Broker and hand over — vendor access migrated to the brokered path, operations handed over
deliverables: Traffic between corporate and control zones traverses the conduit and matches a named rule
A vendor maintenance session is brokered, recorded and revocable without a rule change
The asset inventory states the observation period and what it cannot claim to have seen
effort: 16–24 weeks per plant, driven by outage windows rather than by engineering effort
languages: English delivery; Arabic plant-level documentation on request
